title: Called Before You're Hired
verse: For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand so that we would walk in them.
body: Your vocation didn't start at a job interview. It started before you were born, when God prepared works specifically for you to walk in. A job is what you do to eat. A vocation is what you were made to do. The first shift is seeing your life as assigned, not accidental.
questions: What "prepared work" might God have for you in your current job that you've been overlooking?
How would your attitude at work change if you truly believed God assigned you there?
What's one way you can treat today as a calling instead of just a shift?

title: Work as Worship
verse: Whatever you do, do your work heartily, as for the Lord and not for people,
body: The mop, the spreadsheet, the tattoo machine — all of it can be worship if the heart behind it is aimed at God. Worship isn't just Sunday singing. It's Monday effort offered upward. When your boss isn't watching, God is, and He's the one you're really working for.
questions: What task do you dread most, and how could you offer it to God as worship?
Who is the real "boss" you're working for, and does your effort reflect that?
What's one practical change you can make tomorrow to work "heartily"?

title: The Intentional Morning
verse: And in the early morning, while it was still dark, Jesus got up, left the house, and went away to a secluded place, and prayed there.
body: Jesus ran a ministry that never stopped demanding Him, yet He started alone with the Father. Intentionality begins before the noise. Give God the first of your day, not the leftovers, and watch how the rest of it orders itself.
questions: What currently gets your first 15 minutes, and what would it take to give them to God?
How does your day go differently when you start with prayer vs. when you don't?
What's one distraction you can remove from your mornings this week?

title: Excellence as Witness
verse: Then this Daniel began distinguishing himself among the commissioners and satraps because he possessed an extraordinary spirit, and the king intended to appoint him over the entire kingdom.
body: Daniel didn't preach at work. He outworked everyone, and his excellence forced a pagan king to notice his God. Your skill is a sermon. Be so good at what you do that people have to ask where it comes from.
questions: Where are you doing "good enough" when God deserves your best?
Who at work might be watching your example, and what are they seeing?
What's one skill you can sharpen this month to serve God better through your work?

title: Rest Is Holy
verse: By the seventh day God completed His work which He had done, and He rested on the seventh day from all His work which He had done.
body: God rested, not because He was tired, but to show us rest is part of the design. If you never stop, you're preaching that the world depends on you. Sabbath is a weekly confession: God runs things, I don't.
questions: Do you actually take a full day of rest, or do you just "rest" while still working?
What are you afraid will happen if you stop for a day?
How can you protect a Sabbath rest this week?

title: One Master
verse: No one can serve two masters; for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and wealth.
body: Money makes a terrible god and a good tool. The moment your decisions are driven by the paycheck instead of the calling, you've switched masters. Check who's really signing your orders.
questions: When you make big decisions, is money the loudest voice in the room?
Is there a financial choice you're facing where faith and money disagree?
What would it look like to use money as a tool instead of serving it as a master?

title: Faithful in Small Things
verse: The one who is faithful in a very little thing is also faithful in much; and the one who is unrighteous in a very little thing is also unrighteous in much.
body: God promotes based on faithfulness, not talent. The small, unseen, unthanked tasks are the interview for bigger things. Don't despise the little assignment — it's the doorway. Today, rest in knowing that God sees the small things you do faithfully.

title: Ambition Redeemed
verse: Do nothing from selfishness or empty conceit, but with humility consider one another as more important than yourselves;
body: Ambition isn't the enemy. Selfish ambition is. There's a holy hunger to build, grow, and achieve — when it's aimed at serving others and glorifying God. Check the fuel in your engine.
questions: Is your drive to succeed about being seen or about serving well? Be honest.
What's a goal you're chasing, and who benefits if you reach it?
How can you pursue excellence this week while keeping humility?

title: Your Work Has Dignity
verse: Whether, then, you eat or drink or whatever you do, do all things for the glory of God.
body: There's no sacred/secular split in God's economy. The pastor isn't more holy than the plumber. Every honest work, done for God's glory, carries eternal weight. Stop ranking callings.
questions: Have you been ranking some work as "more spiritual" than others? Where did that come from?
How does seeing your job as God-given change the way you do it?
What's one way you can bring God's glory into an ordinary task today?

title: Planning with Open Hands
verse: The mind of a person plans his way, But the LORD directs his steps.
body: Plan hard, hold loosely. Intentionality means you show up with a plan, but you don't worship it. God's redirections aren't interruptions — they're the actual route.
questions: What's a plan you're gripping too tightly right now?
When God redirected you in the past, did it turn out better? What did you learn?
How can you plan diligently this week while staying open to God's changes?

title: Integrity in the Dark
verse: One who walks in integrity walks securely, But one who perverts his ways will be found out.
body: Character is what you do when the camera's off. Cut the corner when no one's looking, and you've told God exactly what your integrity is worth. Walk clean, especially in the dark.
questions: Is there a shortcut you're taking that you'd be embarrassed about if exposed?
What does your private behavior say about your public faith?
What's one area where you need to "walk securely" by cleaning up your actions?

title: Loving the Difficult
verse: But I say to you, love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,
body: That coworker who drives you crazy is your assignment, not your obstacle. God didn't call you to love the lovely. The difficult person is where your Christianity gets proven.
questions: Who is the most difficult person in your work or life right now?
Have you been complaining about them instead of praying for them?
What's one kind action you can take toward that person this week?

title: The Gift of No
verse: There is an appointed time for everything. And there is a time for every matter under heaven—
body: Saying yes to everything means saying no to what matters. Intentionality requires the courage to decline. Every yes is a thousand nos — make sure you're spending them wisely.
questions: What are you saying yes to that God never asked you to do?
What's suffering because you're overcommitted?
What do you need to decline this week to protect what matters?

title: The Craftsman's Anointing
verse: And I have filled him with the Spirit of God in wisdom, in understanding, in knowledge, and in all kinds of craftsmanship,
body: Bezalel was filled with the Holy Spirit — not to preach, but to build. God anoints craftsmanship. Your hands, your skill, your trade can carry the Spirit's filling just as much as a pulpit. Today, rest and ask God to anoint your hands for the week ahead.

title: Faithful in Obscurity
verse: And the LORD was with Joseph, so he became a successful man. And he was in the house of his master, the Egyptian.
body: Joseph was excellent as a slave, excellent in prison, before he was ever excellent in the palace. God was with him in the pit, not just the palace. Don't wait for the platform to be faithful.
questions: Are you waiting for a bigger platform before giving God your best?
How did Joseph stay faithful without bitterness, and what can you learn from that?
What's your "prison" right now, and how can you serve God excellently in it?

title: Truth with Love
verse: but speaking the truth in love, we are to grow up in all aspects into Him who is the head, that is, Christ,
body: Silence isn't kindness when truth is needed. But truth without love is just a weapon. The intentional Christian learns to say hard things in a way that builds up instead of tearing down.
questions: Is there a hard truth you've been avoiding telling someone who needs to hear it?
When you speak truth, does it sound like love or like a weapon?
How can you have one honest, loving conversation this week you've been putting off?

title: Generosity on Purpose
verse: Each one must do just as he has decided in his heart, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.
body: Decided in your heart — that's intentionality. Not guilt-giving, not pressure-giving, but planned, cheerful, purposeful generosity. Put it in the budget before the budget tells you there's nothing left.
questions: Is your giving planned and cheerful, or reluctant and leftover?
What percentage of your income goes to God first, and is that intentional?
What's one generous act you can plan (not just feel) this week?

title: The Ministry of Presence
verse: do not merely look out for your own personal interests, but also for the interests of others.
body: Sometimes the most spiritual thing you can do is show up and pay attention. Put the phone down. Look people in the eye. Presence is rare, and it's powerful. Be where your feet are.
questions: Who gets your distracted leftovers instead of your real attention?
How often are you physically present but mentally somewhere else?
What's one relationship where you can be fully present this week?

title: Failure Isn't Final
verse: 'Simon, son of John, do you love Me more than these?' He said to Him, 'Yes, Lord; You know that I love You.' He said to him, 'Tend My lambs.'
body: Peter denied Jesus three times, then got restored over breakfast and handed a mission. Your worst failure is not your final chapter. God restores failures and puts them back to work.
questions: What failure are you letting define you that God has already forgiven?
Like Peter, have you been hiding from your calling because of shame?
What's one step you can take this week to get back to the work God gave you?

title: Rhythm Over Hustle
verse: Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy.
body: Hustle says your worth is your output. Sabbath says your worth was settled at the cross. Build a weekly rhythm of rest or burnout will build one for you. The command isn't a suggestion.
questions: Are you building a sustainable rhythm, or are you running on fumes?
What does your exhaustion reveal about what you're trusting in?
What's one boundary you can set this week to protect your rest?

title: Calling Over Career
verse: For am I now seeking the favor of people, or of God? Or am I striving to please people? If I were still trying to please people, I would not be a bond-servant of Christ.
body: A career asks "What will this do for me?" A calling asks "What does God want through me?" When your identity is in your job title, losing the job means losing yourself. Today, rest in the deeper anchor: you are God's before you are anyone's employee.

title: Sharp Friends
verse: As iron sharpens iron, So one person sharpens another.
body: You become like who you spend time with. Intentional Christians choose their circle on purpose. Find people who make you sharper, not duller — who tell you the truth, not just what you want to hear.
questions: Who in your circle makes you sharper, and who makes you duller?
When's the last time someone told you a hard truth because they love you?
Who are you intentionally sharpening, and how?

title: Let Your Yes Be Yes
verse: But make sure your statement is, 'Yes, yes' or 'No, no'; anything beyond these is of evil origin.
body: Reliability is a spiritual discipline. Do what you said you'd do. Show up when you said you'd show up. In a world of flakes, a Christian who keeps their word stands out like a lighthouse.
questions: Is there a commitment you've been half-keeping?
Do people know they can count on your word, or have you been flaky?
What's one promise you need to either fully keep or honestly renegotiate?

title: Audience of One
verse: but just as we have been approved by God to be entrusted with the gospel, so we speak, not intending to please people, but to please God, who examines our hearts.
body: When you work for applause, you're a slave to opinions. When you work for God, you're free. The intentional Christian plays to an audience of one — and that changes everything about how you handle criticism and praise.
questions: Whose approval are you actually working for — God's or people's?
How do you handle criticism? Does it crush you or refine you?
What's one thing you'd do differently if you truly didn't care what people think?

title: Made to Create
verse: So God created man in His own image, in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them.
body: God is a creator, and you're made in His image — which means creativity isn't optional, it's in your DNA. Whether it's art, problem-solving, building, or cooking, creating reflects your Maker. Don't bury that part of you.
questions: What creative gift has God put in you that you've been neglecting?
Are you consuming more than you're creating?
What's one thing you can make, build, or create this week that reflects your Maker?

title: Handling Success
verse: But you are to remember the LORD your God, for it is He who is giving you power to make wealth, in order to confirm His covenant which He swore to your fathers, as it is this day.
body: Success is a test, not just a reward. It reveals whether you remember who gave you the ability. Hold every win with open hands and a grateful heart, or success will become your god.
questions: When things go well, do you get grateful or proud? Be honest.
Do you remember God when you succeed, or only when you struggle?
How can you use a recent win to bless someone else?

title: Receiving Correction
verse: One whose ear listens to a life-giving rebuke Will stay among the wise.
body: The intentional Christian doesn't just tolerate feedback — they hunt for it. Correction is a gift, even when it stings. The person willing to tell you the hard truth is doing you a favor your ego won't.
questions: When's the last time you asked for feedback instead of just receiving it?
Do you get defensive when corrected, or do you listen?
Who can you ask this week: "What do I need to work on?"

title: The Long Obedience
verse: Therefore, since we also have such a great cloud of witnesses surrounding us, let's rid ourselves of every obstacle and the sin which so easily entangles us, and let's run with endurance the race that is set before us,
body: Faithfulness isn't a sprint, it's a long obedience in the same direction. Most people quit right before the breakthrough. Today, rest and remember: the race is won by those who don't stop. You're still in it.

title: Living for Legacy
verse: We will not conceal them from their children, But we will tell the generation to come the praises of the LORD, And His power and His wondrous works that He has done.
body: You're writing a story someone else will read. What you do with your vocation, your integrity, your intentionality — it's teaching the next generation what a genuine Christian looks like. Live like someone's watching, because they are.
questions: What story is your work life telling the next generation?
If someone followed you for a week, what would they learn about following Jesus?
What's one thing you want to be remembered for, and are you living it now?

title: Eyes on Eternity
verse: while we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen; for the things which are seen are temporal, but the things which are not seen are eternal.
body: Every deadline, every paycheck, every project is temporary. The intentional Christian works with eternity in view — not ignoring the present, but never mistaking it for the whole story. Live today in light of forever.
questions: If you really believed this life is temporary, what would you stop worrying about?
What are you investing in that will outlast you?
What's one eternal-perspective decision you can make this week?
